Recursion is a programming technique where a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of that same problem. Every recursive function needs a "base case" — a simple condition that stops the calling and returns a direct answer, preventing an infinite loop. For example, calculating factorial(5) means multiplying 5 by factorial(4), which multiplies 4 by factorial(3), and so on until you reach factorial(1), which simply returns 1. Once the base case is reached, the answers unwind back through each call, combining to produce the final result.
